result:
Issue discovery now checks every proposed deduplication group before it changes anything. A malformed group is skipped in full with a debug-level log entry and is no longer able to crash a run or merge the wrong issues. All 67 tests in `tests/genai/discovery/test_pipeline.py` pass.

**What changed** (`mlflow/genai/discovery/pipeline.py`):
- **New check:** `_is_valid_dedup_group(indices, num_issues)` passes a group only if it has at least two references, none repeated, none negative and all within the candidate list.
- **Where it runs:** `_dedup_issues` calls this check first for each group, in place of the old check that only counted references. A group that fails is skipped entirely: it joins no issues and its name, description and root cause are not applied. Dropping only the bad references was ruled out because the description would then describe a different set of issues.
- **Effect on candidates:** a skipped group touches nothing, so its candidate issues stay available to other valid groups. The result is the same whichever order the groups come in.
- **Unchanged:** valid groups work as before, including overlapping groups that merge transitively, and merged issues keep all their example indices. The existing deduplication tests pass unchanged.

**New test** (`tests/genai/discovery/test_pipeline.py`): `test_dedup_issues_skips_malformed_groups` runs six bad groups alongside a valid `[1, 2]` group, with the bad group placed both before and after the valid one. The bad groups are out of range (`[0, 3]`), negative (`[-1, 0]`), a repeat (`[0, 0]`), a repeat inside an otherwise distinct group (`[2, 2, 0]`), a single reference and an empty group. Each case checks that the valid merge is applied with its own name, description and examples, and that issue 0 is left untouched.

I didn't run the new test against the old code to watch it fail first. Ruff isn't installed in the venv, so I didn't run it and instead formatted one line by hand to match its style. The change already staged in `tests/store/tracking/...` was there before I started; I left it alone.

diff --git a/mlflow/genai/discovery/pipeline.py b/mlflow/genai/discovery/pipeline.py
index f8cf1194c..0cea633f5 100644
--- a/mlflow/genai/discovery/pipeline.py
+++ b/mlflow/genai/discovery/pipeline.py
@@ -357,6 +357,19 @@ class _DedupGroups(pydantic.BaseModel):
     )
 
 
+def _is_valid_dedup_group(indices: list[int], num_issues: int) -> bool:
+    """
+    Check that a dedup group references at least two distinct, in-range issue indices.
+    Malformed groups are rejected as a whole rather than partially applied, since the
+    consolidated name/description were written for the full (invalid) set of indices.
+    """
+    return (
+        len(indices) >= 2
+        and len(set(indices)) == len(indices)
+        and all(0 <= idx < num_issues for idx in indices)
+    )
+
+
 def _dedup_issues(
     issues: list[_IdentifiedIssue],
     model: str = DEFAULT_MODEL,
@@ -394,7 +407,8 @@ def _dedup_issues(
 
     group_by_root: dict[int, _DedupGroup] = {}
     for group in result.groups:
-        if len(group.indices) < 2:
+        if not _is_valid_dedup_group(group.indices, len(issues)):
+            _logger.debug("Skipping malformed dedup group with indices %s", group.indices)
             continue
         root = min(group.indices)
         group_by_root[root] = group
diff --git a/tests/genai/discovery/test_pipeline.py b/tests/genai/discovery/test_pipeline.py
index bc78a49bd..c48dc872b 100644
--- a/tests/genai/discovery/test_pipeline.py
+++ b/tests/genai/discovery/test_pipeline.py
@@ -1289,3 +1289,40 @@ def test_dedup_issues_llm_failure_returns_original():
     with patch("mlflow.genai.discovery.pipeline._call_llm", side_effect=Exception("API error")):
         result = _dedup_issues(issues)
     assert result == issues
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize(
+    "invalid_indices",
+    [
+        [0, 3],  # out of range
+        [-1, 0],  # negative
+        [0, 0],  # repeated
+        [2, 2, 0],  # repeated within otherwise distinct group
+        [1],  # fewer than two
+        [],
+    ],
+)
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("invalid_first", [True, False])
+def test_dedup_issues_skips_malformed_groups(invalid_indices, invalid_first):
+    issues = [
+        create_identified_issue(
+            name=f"Issue: {i}", description=f"desc {i}", example_indices=[i], severity="low"
+        )
+        for i in range(3)
+    ]
+    groups = [invalid_indices, [1, 2]] if invalid_first else [[1, 2], invalid_indices]
+    names = ["Issue: Bad", "Issue: Good"] if invalid_first else ["Issue: Good", "Issue: Bad"]
+    descriptions = ["Bad desc", "Good desc"] if invalid_first else ["Good desc", "Bad desc"]
+    with patch(
+        "mlflow.genai.discovery.pipeline._call_llm",
+        return_value=_make_dedup_response(groups, names=names, descriptions=descriptions),
+    ):
+        result = _dedup_issues(issues)
+
+    assert len(result) == 2
+    assert result[0].name == "Issue: 0"
+    assert result[0].description == "desc 0"
+    assert result[0].example_indices == [0]
+    assert result[1].name == "Issue: Good"
+    assert result[1].description == "Good desc"
+    assert set(result[1].example_indices) == {1, 2}
